question: Should `socket.drain` become a public Gateway event that may close slow existing session subscribers, or should the fix stay narrower and preserve the current `sessions.changed` backpressure contract?
rationale: The duplicate helper is mechanical, but the public event and slow-subscriber behavior are Gateway protocol and compatibility choices that automation should not decide silently.

options.title: Narrow compatible drain
options.body: Keep the message-subscriber repair, document the event if it remains advertised, and preserve current `sessions.subscribe` slow-consumer behavior unless explicitly opted into a new close-on-slow path.

options.title: Approve fail-closed drain
options.body: Accept `socket.drain` as a public fail-closed lifecycle event, but require docs, client handling, and tests proving the intentional disconnect behavior.

options.title: Pause the public event
options.body: Hold or close this direction until maintainers decide whether a separate public Gateway drain event belongs in the protocol.

recommendation.title: Narrow compatible drain
recommendation.body: Keep the message-subscriber repair, document the event if it remains advertised, and preserve current `sessions.subscribe` slow-consumer behavior unless explicitly opted into a new close-on-slow path.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked session-management PR introduced the central session lifecycle/message event surface, making this the closest history-backed routing candidate.
